finding: A generated-hostname observation should not accept an unstructured prose report or a bare HTTP status. A retained curl --write-out JSON receipt can be promoted only when the command itself proves HEAD-only operation, zero redirect allowance, normal TLS verification, exact generated-hostname targeting, and machine-readable transfer metrics.

primary_sources.title: curl man page
observations: --write-out %{json} emits a JSON object containing available transfer keys.
url_effective reports the last fetched URL.
ssl_verify_result equal to 0 means peer certificate verification succeeded.
method, response_code, and time_total are available write-out variables.

uncertainty: No live Vercel generated hostname was requested.
The exact curl version in the eventual authenticated checkout was not observed.
A successful receipt proves only a direct HTTPS response at the generated hostname, not content correctness, alias promotion, browser behavior, audio, or physical-device behavior.
falsification_route: Run the documented curl command against an immutable verified deployment hostname.
Retain the exact command array, raw %{json} output, exit code, and observation time.
Reject the receipt if the installed curl lacks required write-out fields or reports nonzero TLS verification, redirects, URL divergence, transfer failure, or non-2xx status.
Independently compare the retained raw metrics with the normalized receipt digest.
